session_covered: US and European sessions of Thursday 1 October
intro: Covers the US/European session of Thursday 1 October. Caveat: at 05:39 AEST the US cash session had not yet closed (close ≈06:00 AEST), so US figures are the latest available intraday prints, not final closes. The AFR column and a Friday SPI 200 figure could not be retrieved.
footnotes: US 10-year Treasury yield: the email gave "~5.24–5.34%** not available", which isn't a single figure, so it isn't shown in full.

Intraday, about 15:26 EDT (Yahoo Finance); US close not yet reached at time of writing. Brent from TheStreet (~14:48 EDT); gold is the futures price.  Sources disagree (Yahoo 5.24%, TheStreet 5.33%, intraday peak ~5.34%); change not reconciled.  As at ASX close Thursday (ABC).

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures for Friday: not available (could not be verified against two sources), so no implied open is given. The ASX 200 closed Thursday at 8,614, down 1.99% (174.9 points), its lowest since mid-June, with every sector lower. US indices were marginally higher intraday.

local_events: Bendigo Bank's 0.25-point variable home loan rate rise, following the RBA's recent hike, takes effect 7 October.
what_moved: US stocks were slightly higher intraday, led by technology after Micron beat estimates and raised guidance. Offsetting that, the 10-year Treasury yield touched about 5.34%, the highest since 2002, and Brent rose above US$100/bbl on Middle East tensions and a Chinese fuel export suspension. Energy outperformed and banks lagged (about -0.7%); S&P 500 sector percentages are not available.

news.headline: US 10-year yield hits highest since 2002.
news.summary: The yield briefly touched about 5.34% and the 30-year about 5.67% after the worst quarter for bonds in decades.

news.headline: ASX 200 falls 1.99% on oil, yields and domestic outlook.
news.summary: More than A$50 billion was wiped from the market, with concern over house prices and elevated interest rates.

news.headline: Softer US PCE inflation fails to hold gains.
news.summary: Headline PCE slowed to 3.4% versus 3.7% expected, but Wednesday's rally reversed late, and Minneapolis Fed's Kashkari said inflation remains too high.

news.headline: Oil jumps on China fuel export suspension.
news.summary: Brent rose about 2.6% to around US$100.60/bbl intraday, with WTI near US$92.

news.headline: US jobless claims fall to 197,000.
news.summary: The fourth straight weekly decline, ahead of Friday's payrolls report.

news.headline: Micron lifts AI-demand sentiment.
news.summary: Micron reported a large earnings beat and guided first-quarter revenue well above expectations, supporting tech.

coming_up: US non-farm payrolls report, Friday 2 October (US time), which is Saturday 3 October in Australia.
